chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Sa'id ibn Yasal, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about leaning (tuk'a) in prayer against the wall on the right and left, so he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lean against a wall during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *tuka'ah* (leaning) against a wall on either the right or left side during prayer, a practical ruling often discussed in the context of physical weakness or limited space. By affirming 'la ba'sa' (no harm), Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that such leaning does not constitute a defect or invalidator of the prayer, distinguishing it from excessive movement that might break concentration. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for accommodating worshippers who may find standing rigidly difficult, ensuring the validity of their devotion without imposing undue hardship.
